chapter: Apollo Bar, Apollo managers and Harlem nightlife
title: Oscar Pettiford as 'the Whaley brothers' and the Apollo Bar
summary: He hired Pettiford for a 46th Street spot, they were the Whaley brothers, and Hinton praises him as the man who followed Blanton.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then we went down to on 46th Street, I had Oscar Pettiford.
46th and what.
Between 6th and 7th, over the -- Louis Apozza had a place over there. And we had -- I had --
46th between 6th and 7th.

I don't know where it was now, but anyway it was over there and we used to fill them up and the man closed the place up to make it larger, see and then Oscar, he would get to the bar and instead of -- he'd tell me get the people out, I said they're waiting for you. He went back to Birdland, the man fired him and then he went back to Birdland. He was making a good salary up there.

He made some great records, Oscar Pettiford, I mean he was a bass player that really truly followed Blanton and carried Blanton, that Blanton could do, Oscar is the one that carried it on to bring bass up to where it is today, don't you believe that.
Oh, he could play that bass. I used to -- I told Duke when I heard about it, I said Pettiford is a soloist, well, he going to play in my band. Yeah, he and I, the Whaley brothers.
Is that what youcalled it.

Yeah, we used to go as the Whaley brothers. And we had a -- up there in Boston, I had a drummer, used to call the Whaley brothers, he and I. But that Apollo bar, that was a -- everybody used to come up there.
That was at --
It was on 8th Avenue near 126th, wasn't it.
No, it was -- the Apollo bar was below the Apollo Theatre.
Oh, yes, you're right.
Right at the corner of one of those -- of St. Nicholas, I think.
That's right, it was near -- on 125th Street near St. Nicholas. Nipsy Russell and Billy Daniels and everybody played there, didn't they. Even Pearl Bailey played there one time, didn't she.
Yeah, that was a good place.
It was a swinging joint.
I used to sit at the bar with the man, the man would put on -- put Cognac out there, I'd drink, I was drinking Cognac see, taking it easy.

Tom, you were really a big dog to us at the time because you had been therebefore all of us come there and you had controls, you really knew that town and you were the kind of guy that could give us all some work, just like you said, you told the guy at the Apollo bar, get Johnny Hodges. It was through you that a lot of us got little gigs now and then.
Yeah, I used to tell a lot of them people. I'd go around, I'd tell them -- they'd want to know who to get and I'd tell them. Man, you get this guy, he's great.
